# Reminders (Apple, App Store ID 1108187841) — Full Review Analysis

**Corpus:** all **25,951** text reviews in `Native Store Reviews/1. Reminders - Don’t forget. Use Reminders/reviews.jsonl`
**Window:** 2021-09-21 → 2026-09-18 (1,824 days) · **Storefronts:** 144 · **Corpus mean rating: 3.9399★**
**Developer:** Apple Inc. (bundle `com.apple.reminders`) · **Price:** free, pre-installed, no in-app purchase, no ads
**Extraction:** 2026-09-20 (`manifest.json`, source `itunes MZStore userReviewsRow`)
**Method:** every review read individually in its original language; 159 hand-assigned theme codes in 10 families and 10 composite unions; a generated theme→ID map validated by six programmatic integrity checks; 34 mechanical absence/presence tests; script family derived mechanically.

**Decision this informs:** whether to build a habit-tracking product against a free, pre-installed first-party incumbent — what that incumbent already wins on, where it structurally fails habit users, and whether any of those failures is a *painkiller* people would pay to remove.

---

## How to read this

Every quantified claim carries a **count, a percentage, the denominator, the market scope, the time window, a signal label and exact review IDs**. Review IDs are `review_id` values from `reviews.jsonl`; the bracketed `#n` is the working index (date order, ties broken by review ID) used by Part 10, so any number resolves to specific reviews and any review resolves to the findings it supports. §9.J lists every review ID behind every code.

Theme counts are **non-exclusive** — a five-star review that praises shared grocery lists and asks for a streak counter is counted in both. Composite unions (`U_` prefix) count each review **once**. Unless a sentence names a narrower scope, the denominator is **25,951 reviews, all 144 storefronts, 2021-09-21 → 2026-09-18**. Segment rates are always written "n of N" and labelled as segment rates.

Translations of non-English quotes are the analyst's own and are marked *[in brackets]*.

### ⚠️ Eight warnings before any number here is used

1. **These reviewers are far more negative than Reminders' actual users.** The same 144 storefronts carry **2,848,718 public ratings** averaging **4.8116★**. This corpus averages **3.9399★** — a gap of **+0.87★**. Text reviews are **0.911%** of all ratings. Nobody opens a pre-installed app to praise it; they open the App Store page to complain, or because a prompt asked them. Treat every negative rate here as an upper bound on the real population and every positive rate as a lower bound (§6.7).
2. **Everything before September 2023 is a survivorship sample, not a sample.** E1 (2021-09-21 → 2023-09-17) holds 2,815 reviews at mean **2.419★**; every later era sits at **4.11–4.15★**. E1 reviews carry **13× the helpful-vote rate** (0.891 votes/review vs 0.061–0.067) and a **32% longer median body** (115 vs 76–87 chars). That is the signature of a feed that retained the most-voted old reviews and dropped the rest — and helpful votes skew negative. **Do not read "ratings improved after iOS 17" into this corpus.** Era comparisons in Part 7 are run with and without E1 (§7.1, §9.D).
3. **This is a listing with no version field and one-line release notes.** Links between a release and what reviewers say are **timing, not proven cause** — except where reviewers say "after the update" themselves (`BUGREPORT_VER` = 219, 0.84%).
4. **One three-month window holds a disproportionate share of the anger.** 2025-12-01 → 2026-02-28 holds 974 reviews (3.75%) at mean **3.41★**, of which **331 (34.0%)** are one- or two-star. Inside it `NEG_UPDATE` runs at 30.60% against a 6.75% global rate. §9.D re-runs every headline without it.
5. **The app is free and has no paywall, so Part 5 is not a conversion analysis.** `MON_WOULD_PAY` = **11 reviews (0.04%)** — below the ignore-by-default threshold. The monetisation evidence here is about money *leaving* to third parties and money *saved* by not leaving, not about revenue from this app.
6. **"Habit tracking" is a lens applied to a task app, not a category the app claims.** Apple does not market Reminders as a habit tracker. `U_HABIT_ANY` = 4,906 (18.90%) records people using it *as one* or asking it to *become one*; that is a read of user behaviour, not of product positioning (§3.3, §9.A).
7. **Storefront is not language and not nationality.** 50 of 144 storefronts reach the 50-review threshold and hold 25,058 reviews (96.56%); 94 storefronts hold 893 (3.44%) and 19 have exactly one review. Script family is derived mechanically: 83.18% Latin, 16.66% non-Latin (§6.6).
8. **No astroturfing, and no incentive language.** Zero reviews are flagged edited; the most prolific author appears twice; only 169 reviews (0.65%) share normalised text with another, all of them phrases of 60 characters or fewer ("good good", "好 好"); the referral/promo-code test returns **zero** hits (§9.H).

# PART 0 — READ THIS FIRST

## 0.1 The moat is not features. It is being already there, free, and wired into the OS

**`U_PRAISE_ANY` = 14,626 (56.36%, mean 4.75★, High-priority signal).** What reviewers actually name:

| Code / union | n | % of 25,951 | Mean | What it records |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `PR_ORGANISE` | 2,676 | 10.31% | 4.88★ | lists, sections, "organises my life" |
| `SEG_MEMORY` | 2,192 | 8.45% | 4.88★ | "I forget things"; the app is external memory |
| `DEPEND` | 1,813 | 6.99% | 4.59★ | "couldn't live without it" |
| `PR_EASY` | 1,546 | 5.96% | 4.88★ | easy, intuitive |
| `PR_GROCERY` | 1,371 | 5.28% | 4.47★ | shopping lists specifically |
| `PR_NOTIF` | 1,126 | 4.34% | 4.91★ | the reminder fired and it worked |
| `PR_SIMPLE` | 1,049 | 4.04% | 4.77★ | not bloated |
| `PR_PROGRESS` | 797 | 3.07% | 4.90★ | ticking things off, staying on track |
| `PR_BETTER_THAN` | 722 | 2.78% | 4.84★ | explicitly better than a named alternative |
| `PR_ENOUGH` | 645 | 2.49% | 4.70★ | "does everything I need", no more wanted |
| `PR_BUILTIN` | 555 | 2.14% | 4.51★ | ships with the phone; nothing to download |
| `PR_FREE` | 271 | 1.04% | 4.79★ | costs nothing, no subscription, no ads |
| `PR_GENERIC` | 5,044 | 19.44% | 4.85★ | approval with no named reason |

**`U_FREE_VALUE` = 902 (3.48%, mean 4.60★, Very strong signal)** — the union of `PR_FREE`, `PR_BUILTIN`, `MON_FREE_VALUE` and `MON_CANCEL_3P`. This is the competitive threat stated in users' own words, and it is not "it's cheap". It is *"why would I install anything else"*.

`14105839959` (#22949, 2026-05-25, cz, 5★) — "Its free, smart, minimalistic, and its from apple". `11301062474` (#9829, 2024-05-24, ca, 5★) — "Why pay for a reminders app? It integrates seamlessly with other Apple apps". `10714706638` (#5810, 2023-12-19, gb, 5★) — "I see no reason to buy a lists app when this is included in iOS". `12918850369` (#17826, 2025-07-21, sg, 5★) — "There are some apps that need to pay to get the vip. This app is free and it has all the things that other apps have". `13935750798` (#21909, 2026-04-08, mx, 5★) — "no tienes que pagar nada, ya viene incluida… Algo gratis no lo encuentras en otras plataformas sin anuncios" *[you don't have to pay anything, it comes included… you won't find something free on other platforms without ads]*.

**`PR_BETTER_THAN` = 722 (2.78%, mean 4.84★)** is a switch that already happened. The cleanest are `14318328707` (#24345, 2026-07-18, in, 5★) — "For anyone looking for a clean, reliable, and easy-to-use task manager, it's an excellent choice"; `14478140980` (#25375, 2026-08-27, gb, 5★) — "I've tried all of the popular reminder apps (google tasks, tick tick, Microsoft to do etc) and none of them come close to the simplicity and integration of this… If you're already in the ecosystem, just do yourself a favour and stick with this one."

**A product competing here is not competing on features. It is competing against zero friction, zero cost and OS-level placement.**

## 0.2 Reliability, not missing features, is what makes people leave

**`U_RELIABILITY` = 6,260 (24.12%, mean 2.32★, High-priority signal)** — a quarter of the corpus reports something broken. It accounts for **3,693 of the 5,315 one- and two-star reviews (69.48%, segment rate)**.

| Code | n | % | Mean | What breaks |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `NEG_UPDATE` | 1,751 | 6.75% | 2.13★ | "it worked until the update" |
| `NEG_NOTIF_FAIL` | 848 | 3.27% | 1.77★ | the reminder never fired |
| `NEG_DATALOSS` | 692 | 2.67% | 1.99★ | reminders or lists vanished |
| `NEG_WIDGET_BUG` | 684 | 2.64% | 2.61★ | widget stale, or a mis-tap completes a task |
| `NEG_SYNC` | 658 | 2.54% | 2.22★ | devices disagree |
| `NEG_CRASH` | 619 | 2.39% | 1.93★ | freezes or quits |
| `NEG_SLOW` | 559 | 2.15% | 2.30★ | seconds to open, seconds to tick |
| `NEG_RECUR_BUG` | 493 | 1.90% | 2.53★ | repeats fire wrong, or self-complete |
| `NEG_SHARED_BUG` | 408 | 1.57% | 2.25★ | shared list does not propagate |

The severity is set by what the app is used for. `13496927280` (#20236, 2025-12-10, gb, 1★) — "It keeps making appointments as completed (even future ones)… me missing out on so many important appointments and medication times". `13629366055` (#20548, 2026-01-13, us, 1★) — "Constantly crashes, is super slow when it does work. I'm neurodivergent and have memories issues so this app has been a vital part of my days".

**This is the single most transferable lesson for a competitor: in this category an unreliable reminder is worse than no reminder, because the user has already stopped holding the information themselves.** `DEPEND` = 1,813 (6.99%) people say they cannot function without it; 248 of them (13.68%, segment rate) also report something broken.

## 0.3 The habit-tracking gap is real, specific, and has been stable for five years

**`U_HABIT_ANY` = 4,906 (18.90%, mean 4.38★, High-priority signal)** use Reminders for habits, routines, medication, chores, study or workouts, or ask it to support them.
**`U_HABIT_TRACK_GAP` = 1,163 (4.48%, mean 3.64★, Very strong signal)** name a specific thing a habit tracker does that Reminders does not.

| Code | n | % | Mean | The gap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `REQ_FLEXFREQ` | 364 | 1.40% | 3.44★ | repeat rules too rigid (every 3 days, after completion, Mon+Fri only, N times) |
| `HAB_NOHIST` | 261 | 1.01% | 3.83★ | no usable history of what was done |
| `REQ_PROGRESS` | 180 | 0.69% | 4.03★ | wants to see completion as progress |
| `HAB_FAIL` | 159 | 0.61% | 2.67★ | tried to build a habit with it and it did not stick |
| `REQ_RESET` | 122 | 0.47% | 3.59★ | wants a daily list that resets instead of disappearing |
| `REQ_REWARD` | 119 | 0.46% | 4.38★ | wants a sound, an animation, a payoff on completion |
| `REQ_HABITMODE` | 109 | 0.42% | 4.05★ | asks outright for a habit-tracker mode |
| `REQ_PARTIAL` | 85 | 0.33% | 3.85★ | wants skip / pause / "not done" as distinct from delete |
| `REQ_STREAK` | 43 | 0.17% | 4.28★ | asks for a streak or a counter |

**The mechanism users describe is the same every time: completion destroys the record.** `13530375297` (#20326, 2025-12-19, ae, 4★) — "It would be very nice if this app got more handy as a habit tracker app… i don't have to delete my previous done tasks to write a new list everyday… be able to check my progress throughout the month or year". `13799906358` (#21079, 2026-02-28, au, 3★) — "when I click on the reminder to say I've done it it just refreshes and shows not done… Should get a line put through it and then refresh at a set time every night… might have to try another app". `11208901802` (#9277, 2024-04-28, gb, 3★) — "when you have daily reminders, it's so disheartening seeing the reminders still there once you've completed for the day". `13962894485` (#22046, 2026-04-16, cn, 4★) — "要是打卡完显示已完成就好了…不然设定的长期目标，不显示今日打卡完成，就造成多次打卡" *[if it showed 'done' after checking in it would be fine… otherwise for a long-term goal it doesn't show today's check-in as complete, so you end up checking in several times]*.

**And they say explicitly that this is why they install a second app.** `10640313176` (#5062, 2023-11-30, in, 5★) — "Can you please build in a streak tracker for periodic reminders… I then do not need to go to third party habit tracker apps". `12648138253` (#16752, 2025-05-12, lt, 5★) — "Norėčiau galėti sekti savo progresą atlikus tam tikras pasikartojančias užduotis… Tada nereiktų jokių papildomų kvailų programėlių sekti savo progresui" *[I'd like to track my progress on recurring tasks… then I wouldn't need any extra silly apps to track my progress]*. `13166724162` (#18749, 2025-09-21, in, 3★) — "It only needs an habit tracker". `14038434827` (#22485, 2026-05-07, eg, 3★) — "ياريت يبقا في تتبع اداء مثل مخطط بياني عشان الناس الي عندها روتين و عادات يوميه" *[I wish there were performance tracking like a chart, for people with routines and daily habits]*.

**Timing matters: this gap is not new and is not closing.** `U_HABIT_TRACK_GAP` runs 3.45–6.16% of reviews in every quarter from 2023Q4 to 2026Q3 with no trend. Five years of requests, unshipped.

## 0.4 Reminders shipped the one painkiller that mattered — and it changed behaviour

The dominant complaint of 2021–2024 was that a reminder appears once and vanishes. `NEG_NOTIF_ONCE` = 326 (1.26%, mean 3.05★); `REQ_ALARM` = 668 (2.57%, mean 3.50★) asked for an alarm-strength alert.

`10534957489` (#4197, 2023-10-31, us, 3★) — "the reminder notifications are too short, quiet, and easy to pass by… They need to function like an alarm, where they don't stop going off until you manually stop it". `10926424943` (#7216, 2024-02-11, de, 4★) — "Die erinnerungen sind nicht aggressiv genug konfigurierbar… der mich so lange richtig stark nervt bis mein Handy akku leer ist oder ich auf 'Erledigt' gedrückt habe" *[reminders can't be configured aggressively enough… one that really pesters me until my battery is dead or I press 'Done']*.

Apple shipped "Urgent" reminders with an alarm. **`REQ_ALARM` mentions rose from 2.28% (2025Q1) to 3.59% (2025Q4) and hold at 3.49–3.50% through 2026Q3 — but the valence flipped from request to praise**, and the reviews say the feature converted non-users into users:

`13965378648` (#22060, 2026-04-16, it, 5★) — "Adoro i nuovi promemoria urgenti, usavo la sveglia prima per cose importanti… ora ho iniziato ad usare seriamente l'app promemoria grazie a questa funzione… prima inutile ora ESSENZIALE" *[I love the new urgent reminders, I used to use the alarm clock for important things… now I've started using Reminders seriously thanks to this feature… useless before, ESSENTIAL now]*. `13461201222` (#20111, 2025-12-01, us, 5★) — "Reminders were so easy to ignore or dismiss before… adding an option to annoy me until I complete the reminder". `14082843382` (#22779, 2026-05-19, ua, 5★) — "круто, що додали можливість ставити «терміновість»… звичайні нагадування у вигляді вспливаючих вікон не мають майже сенсу" *[great that they added 'urgency'… ordinary pop-up reminders make almost no sense]*. `14030125965` (#22435, 2026-05-05, in, 5★) — "The reminder's Urgent feature and integration with Calendar has leveled it up".

**Read this as the category's proof of what a painkiller looks like here: not more organisation, but making the alert impossible to ignore.** It is also a warning — the same mechanism produced §0.5.

## 0.5 The same painkiller, delivered as a permission nag, cost three months of goodwill

From **2025-12-01 to 2026-02-28** the corpus falls to mean **3.41★** (974 reviews, 3.75% of the corpus; 331 of them one- or two-star = 34.0%, segment rate). Inside the window, `NEG_UPDATE` = 298 (30.60% of the window vs 6.75% globally) and `NEG_BUG` = 261 (26.80% vs 5.81%). Monthly, `NEG_UPDATE` runs 5.20% (Nov) → 22.73% (Dec) → **38.94% (Jan)** → 29.84% (Feb) → 4.81% (Mar).

The cause reviewers name is a full-screen "Allow Alarms for Urgent Reminders" prompt that could not be dismissed. `13679966167` (#20711, 2026-01-27, ru, 1★) — "невозможно закрыть «Разрешите звуковые сигналы для срочных напомина-ний»" *[impossible to close "Allow sounds for urgent reminders"]*. `13655134887` (#20636, 2026-01-20, ru, 1★) — "проблеме со всплывающим окном, которое невозможно закрыть" *[problem with a pop-up window that can't be closed]*. `13722347430` (#20833, 2026-02-07, de, 1★) — "Hinweis für dringende Erinnerungen lässt sich nicht deaktivieren" *[the notice for urgent reminders can't be switched off]*. `13738069014` (#20871, 2026-02-11, ru, 1★) — "Выскакивает банер о звуковом сигнале на весь экран" *[a full-screen banner about the alert sound pops up]*. `13615018461` (#20514, 2026-01-10, us, 1★) — "they app has a notification that pops up and blocs the other buttons". `13771235320` (#20964, 2026-02-20, jp, 2★) — "リマインダーを開くたびに「アラームへのアクセスがオフになっている」とメッセージが出る…結局、他に乗り換えることにした" *[every time I open Reminders a message says "alarm access is off"… in the end I decided to switch to something else]*.

A second nag runs alongside it: location permission. `NEG_NOTIF_NAG` peaks at **6.78% in January 2026** against 0.74% globally. `13688607433` (#20743, 2026-01-29, de, 1★) — "Bei jeden öffnen muss man die Standortfreigabe erneut ablehnen" *[on every open you have to decline location sharing again]*. `14499495958` (#25521, 2026-09-01, dk, 1★) quotes the dialog verbatim and adds "I thought Apple was a company focused on privacy???"

**The lesson is exact: the feature that drove §0.4 and the regression that drove §0.5 are the same feature. Permission-gated alerting is a painkiller when it is opt-in once and a churn event when it is a blocking prompt on every launch.**

## 0.6 Almost nobody will pay, and that is the finding — the money is already spent elsewhere

| Code | n | % of 25,951 | Mean | What it records |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `MON_FREE_VALUE` | 387 | 1.49% | 4.80★ | free/built-in is why they use it |
| `MON_REFUSE_PAY` | 97 | 0.37% | 4.56★ | explicitly says don't pay for this category |
| `MON_PAID_3P` | 68 | 0.26% | 4.18★ | says they paid, or pay, a third party |
| `MON_CANCEL_3P` | 37 | 0.14% | 4.84★ | cancelled a paid app *for* Reminders |
| `MON_WOULD_PAY` | 11 | 0.04% | 2.91★ | would pay for something |
| `MON_PAID_ICLOUD` | 9 | 0.03% | 3.22★ | mentions paying for iCloud |

**`MON_WOULD_PAY` = 11 (0.04%) is below the ignore-by-default threshold.** It is reported here only because the question was asked directly, and because *what* those eleven say is more useful than the count. Nine of the eleven are not offers to pay Apple — they are threats to pay someone else over one missing thing:

`8983501166` (#1520, 2022-08-16, us, 2★) — "This app is essentially included with the cost of my iPhone, so I expect more from it… I therefore have to pay another company $60 annually… **If Apple would just create this ONE feature, I would abandon my other app**". `10888706654` (#6931, 2024-02-01, us, 1★) — daily reminders being deleted — "I'm so ready to spend extra money on a app that we get the job done". `11537739515` (#11228, 2024-07-26, us, 2★) — "Not enough ranges for repeats, doesn't always sync across devices… thinking of paying for a app that can do all of this better".

Only two are willingness to pay *for Reminders*: `9154506457` (#1709, 2022-10-05, nl, 5★) — "If it wasn't free I'd pay for it"; `11845527226` (#12898, 2024-10-18, fr, 5★) — "Si l'app n'était pas gratuite, je n'aurais aucun problème à payer pour l'avoir" *[if the app weren't free I'd have no problem paying for it]*.

And the ceiling is stated plainly: `14522067015` (#25682, 2026-09-07, us, 5★) — "**I can't fathom my anyone would pay $100 a year to use another app. If there was another high-quality Reminders app that I could just pay for once, I would consider it.** Every single app as a huge subscription prize which makes zero sense for the level of this is."

**`MON_CANCEL_3P` = 37 is the counter-flow and it is one-directional money.** `12189828481` (#14601, 2025-01-16, us, 5★) — "All the new features in Reminders mean I'm no longer paying for OmniFocus". `10514522309` (#4039, 2023-10-25, us, 5★) — "I've been an omnifocus user for years and happily paid the subscription fee… the new version is VERY capable and does everything i need. And it's free". `12450118186` (#15881, 2025-03-22, de, 4★) — "Ich habe jahrelang Things genutzt, bin aber nun endgültig umgestiegen… So reicht dann diese App absolut und kostet nichts" *[I used Things for years, but now I've switched for good… this app is completely enough and costs nothing]*. `13627389508` (#20539, 2026-01-13, ca, 5★) — "Finally I'm able to switch from ToDoist". `14137557642` (#23185, 2026-06-03, us, 5★) — "I've ditched Microsoft To Do in favor of Apple's Reminders".

**Conclusion for pricing: in this category a subscription must clear a bar set by a competent free incumbent, and the corpus contains explicit resistance to subscriptions and one explicit preference for a one-time price. A paid habit product cannot be sold as "a better list". It has to be sold as the thing Reminders structurally will not do (§0.3) and cannot be worth $100/year to this audience.**

## 0.7 Leaving is driven by broken trust; staying is driven by capability

Combining `SW_TO_3P`, `SW_CONSIDER` and `HAB_SWITCH_OUT` gives a **leave-intent set of 465 reviews (1.79%, mean 2.06★)**. Against that 1.79% base rate, the codes with the highest co-occurrence are all reliability or trust failures, not feature gaps:

| Code | n | leave-intent | share | lift |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `NEG_NOTIF_ACTION` | 103 | 14 | 13.59% | 7.6× |
| `NEG_CALENDAR` | 146 | 14 | 9.59% | 5.4× |
| `REQ_STREAK` | 43 | 4 | 9.30% | 5.2× |
| `TENURE_LONG` | 432 | 39 | 9.03% | 5.0× |
| `NEG_SUPPORT` | 236 | 18 | 7.63% | 4.3× |
| `NEG_DATALOSS` | 692 | 50 | 7.23% | 4.0× |
| `REQ_SNOOZE` | 196 | 14 | 7.14% | 4.0× |
| `NEG_RECUR_BUG` | 493 | 34 | 6.90% | 3.8× |
| `NEG_NOTIF_FAIL` | 848 | 56 | 6.60% | 3.7× |

At the other end, `PR_RELIABLE` (522), `PR_PROGRESS` (797), `PR_FAST` (300) and `PR_CUSTOM` (206) have **zero** leave-intent overlap.

Two entries deserve attention. **`TENURE_LONG` at 5.0× lift** means long-tenure users are among the most likely to threaten to leave — they have the most to lose from a regression and the most sunk data. **`REQ_STREAK` at 5.2× lift on only 43 reviews** is a weak count with a strong signal: the handful who want streaks are unusually willing to go elsewhere to get them.

## 0.8 What this corpus shows is *absent*

Mechanical presence tests over title+body (§9.F), every hit read:

- **Gamification vocabulary is essentially absent.** "gamify / dopamine / reward / recompensa / Belohnung / ご褒美" = **15 (0.06%)**. "streak / racha / 連続 / 打卡天数" = **22 (0.08%)**. "statistics / progress bar" = **22 (0.08%)**. These users describe the *outcome* they want (see §0.3) without the habit-app vocabulary — which means keyword-only research on this corpus would have found nothing, and a habit product marketed in that vocabulary may not be recognised by them.
- **Privacy is a non-topic.** 12 reviews (0.05%) mention privacy or data protection at all. `NEG_PRIVACY` = 57 (0.22%), and most of those are the location-permission nag of §0.5, not a data concern.
- **No refund economy.** "refund / remboursement / reembolso" = **2 reviews**. No paywall, so no refunds.
- **No referral or incentive language whatsoever** — 0 hits.
- **Export and backup barely register** — 77 (0.30%), mean 2.48★, and almost all of them are people who had already lost data.
- **Third-party habit apps are named 3 times in 25,951 reviews.** Habitica, Streaks, Habitify, HabitNow, HabitDone, Way of Life and Loop combined: **3 hits**. Task competitors are named far more often (Todoist 59, Google 77, Microsoft To Do 37, Notion 28, Things 26). **Reminders' users do not think of themselves as being in the habit-tracker market.**

# PART 1 — SCOPE AND METHOD

## 1.1 Files used

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `Native Store Reviews/1. Reminders - Don’t forget. Use Reminders/reviews.jsonl` | 25,951 records — the corpus. Every claim resolves here. |
| `…/by_country/*.jsonl` | 144 per-storefront files, used only for reconciliation |
| `…/manifest.json` | totals, per-country counts, rating distribution, extraction stamp |
| `…/_state.json` | per-storefront collection completeness flags |
| `Tools/native_ratings.json` | public rating counts and means per storefront (external comparison, §6.7) |
| `Temp/n1-cls/*.txt` | 260 hand-coded batch files, one line per review — the source of truth for every code |
| `Temp/n1-review-classification.py` | generated theme → review-ID map (§9.J) |

Scripts, all in `Temp/`: `n1-common.py` (loader, signal bands), `n1-dump.py` / `n1-batch/` (reading batches), `n1-fill-ids.py`, `n1-check-cls.py` (per-line validator), `n1-build-classification.py`, `n1-validate.py` (six integrity checks), `n1-stats.py`, `n1-trend.py`, `n1-country.py`, `n1-painkiller.py`, `n1-absence.py`, `n1-script.py`, `n1-ev.py`, `n1-build-report.py`.

## 1.2 Schema actually present

Fields on every record: `app_id`, `app_name`, `author`, `body`, `country`, `country_name`, `date`, `is_edited`, `rating`, `review_id`, `title`, `vote_count`, `vote_sum`.

**Fields that do not exist and therefore cannot be analysed: app version, device, OS version, developer response, purchase state, subscription state.** Every version-linked statement in Part 7 is timing-based or self-reported by the reviewer.

Field quality: `is_edited` is `false` on all 25,951 records. `vote_count` > 0 on 1,276 (4.92%). One review has an empty title; none has an empty body. `author` repeats at most twice.

## 1.3 Coverage and reconciliation

`Temp/n1-reconcile-out.txt`, regenerated for this report:

```
main reviews.jsonl records       : 25951
unique review_id                 : 25951
manifest total_reviews           : 25951
manifest storefronts_with_reviews: 144
distinct countries in main       : 144
country files                    : 144
country files with internal dups : 0
country-file ids absent from main: 0
union of country files           : 25951
main ids absent from country fls : 0
per-country count mismatches     : 0
_state.json mismatches/incomplete: 0
rating distribution main         : {1: 3855, 2: 1460, 3: 2316, 4: 3079, 5: 15241}
rating distribution manifest     : identical
mean rating main / manifest      : 3.9399 / 3.94
date range                       : 2021-09-21 -> 2026-09-18
```

**Coverage is exact: 25,951 of 25,951 read and classified, zero deduplication applied, zero records dropped.**

## 1.4 Processing method

1. **Dump.** `n1-dump.py` wrote the corpus in date order into 260 batch files of 100 reviews (`n1-batch/00001-00100.txt` … `25901-25951.txt`), each record showing index, storefront, stars, date, title and full body.
2. **Read.** Every batch was read in full, in the original language, in both halves. No sampling, no keyword pre-filter, no truncation at a context boundary.
3. **Hand-code.** One line written per review into `n1-cls/<range>.txt` in the form
   `idx ~ CODE,CODE  # lang=xx | "verbatim fragment"; "verbatim fragment"`.
   The `~` was later replaced with the review ID by `n1-fill-ids.py`.
4. **Validate each batch at write time.** `n1-check-cls.py` enforces: index in range and in order; review ID matches the index; every code defined in `n1-themes.py`; no duplicate codes on a line; no duplicate or missing indexes; **and every quoted fragment present verbatim in that review's `title + "\n" + body`** after NFKC and curly-quote normalisation. 36 errors were raised and fixed during coding (unknown codes, duplicate codes after a bulk rename, five mis-transcribed quotes) — §9.C.
5. **Build.** `n1-build-classification.py` inverted the per-line data into `THEMES` (code → review IDs), `UNIONS`, `PER_REVIEW` and `LANG`.
6. **Validate the built map.** `n1-validate.py`, six checks, all passing (§9.C).
7. **Aggregate.** Global, per-rating, per-storefront, per-quarter and per-era tables; leave-intent lift; 34 mechanical absence tests; mechanical script detection.

**Where automation was used and where it was not.** All *counting* is programmatic. All *classification* is by hand. The only mechanically derived attributes are script family (§6.6) and the absence tests (§9.F), both of which are reported as mechanical and whose hits were read.

**Known error risk.** With 159 codes and 63,065 assignments at a mean of 2.43 codes per review, boundary decisions between adjacent codes (`PR_EASY` vs `PR_SIMPLE`; `NEG_BUG` vs `NEG_CRASH`; `REQ_RESET` vs `REQ_HABITMODE`) carry judgement. Unions exist to absorb that: every headline in Part 0 is stated on a union or on a code whose boundary is unambiguous. `PR_GENERIC` (19.44%) and `NOISE` (7.93%) are deliberately large and carry no interpretive weight.

## 1.5 Signal thresholds

| Share of reviews | Label | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Under 0.1% | Ignore by default | Not promoted unless safety, legal, security or severe data-loss |
| 0.1% – <0.5% | Weak | Recorded with cautious wording |
| 0.5% – <1% | Emerging | Worth further investigation |
| 1% – <3% | Meaningful | Strong candidate for product consideration |
| 3% – 5% | Very strong | Should influence roadmap |
| Above 5% | High-priority | Strong product problem or opportunity |

Applied to the global corpus (denominator 25,951) and separately to each of the 50 eligible storefronts with that storefront's own total as denominator. Segment rates (within one-star reviews, within a storefront, within `HAB_USE`) are always labelled and never substituted for the global band.

At this corpus size **0.1% is 26 reviews**, so bands are unusually stable; the tradeoff is that genuinely rare but important patterns (`MON_WOULD_PAY` = 11) fall below threshold and must be reported qualitatively, which §0.6 does explicitly.

## 1.6 Limitations, stated plainly

1. **Severe non-response bias** (§6.7). +0.87★ gap against 2.85M public ratings; 0.911% of raters wrote text.
2. **E1 is survivorship** (§7.1). Pre-September-2023 data cannot support a trend claim.
3. **No version field.** Release attribution is timing plus self-report only.
4. **Storefront ≠ language ≠ nationality** (§6.6).
5. **Hand-coding is one analyst.** No second coder, so no inter-rater agreement statistic is available. Mitigation is the verbatim-quote check (every code is anchored to text that provably exists) and union-level reporting.
6. **"Habit tracking" is an imposed lens** (§9.A). `HAB_*` codes record behaviour the analyst judged to be habit-like; a reviewer saying "I use it every day" is `HAB_DAILY`, which is a usage-frequency claim, not a claim that they are building a habit.
7. **No causal claims.** Star rating is never read as a feature preference, and co-occurrence lift (§0.7) is association, not causation.
8. **The three-month window of §0.5** distorts any un-windowed 2026 statistic; §9.D re-runs the headlines without it.

## 2.2 External facts, kept separate from review evidence

From `Native Store Reviews/.../manifest.json` (extracted 2026-09-20) and `Tools/native_ratings.json`:

- **App Store ID** 1108187841, **bundle** `com.apple.reminders`, **developer** Apple Inc.
- **Public ratings across the 144 storefronts in this corpus: 2,848,718, weighted mean 4.8116★.** Across all 171 storefronts with data: 2,849,749, mean 4.8116★.
- No price, no in-app purchase and no ad SDK is referenced anywhere in the corpus; the ads test (§9.F) returns 97 hits (0.37%) and reading all 97 shows they are (a) people praising the *absence* of ads, (b) people complaining about the review-request prompt, or (c) complaints about ads in *other* apps. **Reminders shows no advertising.**

No other external source was consulted, and no claim in this report depends on one.

## 2.3 Free / paid / trial / unclear — classified

| Classification | What falls in it |
|---|---|
| **Free, unconditionally** | Every capability named in §2.1. No reviewer describes any Reminders feature as locked, trial-limited or upgrade-gated. |
| **Free but requires a paid dependency** | Nothing functionally — but sync depends on iCloud, and 9 reviewers (`MON_PAID_ICLOUD`, 0.03%) connect the two. `12442759289` (#15842, 2025-03-20, ca, 2★) hit the free iCloud storage ceiling; `14193949220` (#23575, 2026-06-17, us, 1★) believed sharing was gated — "Sharing bounces to App Store. Guessing it's to force iCloud backup license" — which is a **misunderstanding**, not a paywall, and is the only such claim in 25,951 reviews. |
| **Paid** | Nothing. |
| **Unclear** | Nothing. |

**There is no paywall, no trial, no upgrade, no ad tier and no premium feature in this product.** That is the whole of §2.3, and it is why Part 5 is reframed.

## 2.4 What could not be established

- Which OS version any reviewer is on (no version field).
- Whether "Urgent reminders" shipped on the date its reviews cluster — only that praise for it appears from 2025Q4 and holds.
- Whether the January 2026 permission banner was a bug or an intended prompt — reviewers report behaviour, not intent.
- Any conversion, retention or revenue figure. None is derivable from review text, and none is given.

## 3.2 What people value, in their own words

**Organisation, not productivity.** `PR_ORGANISE` = 2,676 (10.31%, 4.88★) is the largest specific praise, and it is almost always phrased as relief rather than output. The clearest are `14478140980` (#25375, 2026-08-27, gb, 5★) and `14318328707` (#24345, 2026-07-18, in, 5★) — "It's incredibly simple and has very little friction—you can capture a task in seconds and get back to what you're doing."

**Speed of capture is the feature people describe emotionally.** `PR_FAST` = 300 (1.16%, **4.92★ — the highest mean of any code above 100 reviews**). Paired with `PR_SIRI` = 561 (2.16%, 4.65★), the pattern is: the thought arrives, it is offloaded in seconds, the head is clear again.

**Checking off is the reward, and people say so unprompted.** `PR_PROGRESS` = 797 (3.07%, 4.90★). `12487371429` (#16061, 2025-03-31, in, 5★) — "It is so fun to tick ur tasks after they r completed". `10474590982` (#3771, 2023-10-14, us, 5★) — "I feel very fulfilled when I can mark off that I have achieved my goals". **This matters for a habit product: the reward loop already works. What is missing is that the record of the reward does not persist (§3.3).**

**Enough is a feature.** `PR_ENOUGH` = 645 (2.49%, 4.70★) and `PR_SIMPLE` = 1,049 (4.04%, 4.77★). `11165430952` (#8994, 2024-04-16, es, 5★) — "esta aplicación me permite organizar mi vida de una manera sencilla pero poderosa. No necesito descargar otra aplicación de organización de tareas" *[this app lets me organise my life simply but powerfully. I don't need to download another task-organisation app]*.

## 3.3 Habits: what people actually do with a task app

`U_HABIT_ANY` = 4,906 (18.90%, mean 4.38★). Composition:

| Code | n | % | Mean | What it records |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `HAB_DAILY` | 2,506 | 9.66% | 4.59★ | uses it daily / every day |
| `HAB_USE` | 981 | 3.78% | 4.72★ | describes a specific recurring personal use |
| `HAB_CHORE` | 413 | 1.59% | 4.56★ | household, bills, pets, maintenance |
| `HAB_MED` | 374 | 1.44% | 4.29★ | medication and supplements |
| `HAB_STUDY` | 149 | 0.57% | 4.79★ | school and coursework |
| `HAB_HEALTH` | 144 | 0.55% | 4.72★ | health routines (water, walking, stretching) |
| `HAB_WORKOUT` | 66 | 0.25% | 4.39★ | exercise |
| `HAB_WORKAROUND` | 153 | 0.59% | 3.93★ | bends the app into a tracker it isn't |
| `HAB_SWITCH_IN` | 41 | 0.16% | 4.83★ | adopted it *for* routines, often from another tool |
| `HAB_FAIL` | 159 | 0.61% | 2.67★ | tried and the habit did not stick |

**Medication is the highest-stakes habit in the corpus and the most defensible product beachhead.** `HAB_MED` = 374 (1.44%, meaningful) plus the mechanical medication test at 261 (1.01%). `11594150694` (#11551, 2024-08-10, us, 5★) — "My husband had a heart attack and went from taking no medication to taking 5 twice a day… I set up a reminder for him and it has been wonderful". `14130853092` (#23128, 2026-06-01, us, 5★) — "My daily meds? I never miss them anymore." `11938728252` (#13351, 2024-11-11, mx, 5★) — "con cosas tan simples como tomar medicamentos o vitaminas" *[with things as simple as taking medicines or vitamins]*.

Against that, `12588991225` (#16505, 2025-04-26, us, 1★) states the gap exactly: "I use this as a medication reminder. **The ability to skip or re-schedule a dose should not require me to delete the entire entry.**"

**The workaround pattern is diagnostic.** `HAB_WORKAROUND` = 153 (0.59%) are people substituting Reminders for a tool it isn't. The clearest is `14202530000` (#23622, 2026-06-19, us, 5★) — "I do wish it had the option to pause reminders that I normally use every day, because sometimes I don't need them daily like when I'm on vacation". Vacation mode, skip, pause: the same three asks, from people who would otherwise be habit-app customers.

**`HAB_FAIL` = 159 (0.61%, mean 2.67★) is the failure mode of a task app used as a habit app.** The mechanism is always the same — the reminder is dismissible, so it gets dismissed, and the routine never forms. `10422075108` (#3249, 2023-09-30, us, 3★) — "For some reason I cannot get myself to use it like an everyday thing… I always forget about the reminders app". `14375570423` (#24703, 2026-08-01, ca, 5★) — "Just doesn't get things done for me :(". `14214153425` (#23711, 2026-06-22, de, 4★) — "wenn ich morgens aufstehe, dann vergesse ich diese Liste und benutz sie dann doch nicht" *[when I get up in the morning I forget this list and don't use it after all]*. `12396717043` (#15597, 2025-03-08, us, 5★) names the record problem exactly — "When I forget to mark it (A reminder) off for the day, it tells me I missed a day but when you go to check it off, now you've done it today".

## 3.4 Who these users are, and what they are compensating for

`U_SEG_ANY` = 3,885 (14.97%, 4.72★).

| Segment | n | % | Mean |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `SEG_MEMORY` — self-describes as forgetful | 2,192 | 8.45% | 4.88★ |
| `SEG_WORK` — work / business use | 787 | 3.03% | 4.60★ |
| `SEG_PARENT` — family coordination | 429 | 1.65% | 4.29★ |
| `SEG_STUDENT` — school or university | 363 | 1.40% | 4.69★ |
| `SEG_ELDER` — names their age as the reason | 242 | 0.93% | 4.81★ |
| `SEG_ADHD` — names ADHD / ADD / autism / OCD | 204 | 0.79% | 4.62★ |
| `SEG_DISABILITY` — illness, injury, impairment | 111 | 0.43% | 4.56★ |
| `SEG_CARER` — managing someone else's life | 25 | 0.10% | 4.72★ |

**`SEG_MEMORY` at 8.45% and 4.88★ is the emotional core of the product.** These are not productivity enthusiasts. `10624025125` (#4812, 2023-11-25, us, 5★) — "At 73 yo I call it my 'brain in an app'". `11527763611` (#11174, 2024-07-24, mx, 5★) — "a mi edad se me olvidan las cosas y esto es una forma de programar mi vida a futuro" *[at my age I forget things and this is a way to programme my life ahead]*; `13867839052` (#21488, 2026-03-20, us, 5★) — "I'm a senior citizen and I just figured out how to use the app for my grocery list".

**The accessibility and clinical cases are small in count and large in consequence.** `SEG_DISABILITY` = 111 (0.43%, weak band) but includes multiple sclerosis, traumatic brain injury, seizures, post-surgical memory loss and autism. `14473486772` (#25340, 2026-08-26, gb, 5★) — "After a serious brain injury, my memory and organisation are difficult — this app keeps EVERYTHING on track." `SEG_CARER` = 25 (0.10%, ignore-by-default band) is reported here **only** because the content is safety-relevant: `10868109981` (#6746, 2024-01-27, us, 5★) — "I am a caregiver… for my father who has many health concerns including memory issues"; `14491869918` (#25464, 2026-08-31, au, 5★) — "I am my 93 yo Mums full time carer. 10 years now. Reminders help me with her daily medications."

**`SEG_ADHD` = 204 (0.79%) is the segment most explicitly asking for the habit features.** `10657301519` (#5288, 2023-12-04, us, 5★) — "Habit tracking may be a useful feature… features that may encourage those of us with ADHD to take action". The mechanical ADHD test finds 152 (0.59%), mean 4.55★ — a segment that rates the app *above* corpus average while asking it to become something else.

## 3.5 Reliability, in detail

`U_RELIABILITY` = 6,260 (24.12%, 2.32★); it supplies **69.48% of all one- and two-star reviews** (3,693 of 5,315, segment rate).

**Notifications that do not fire is the most damaging single failure.** `NEG_NOTIF_FAIL` = 848 (3.27%, **1.77★ — the lowest mean of any code above 500 reviews**). For an app whose entire promise is one thing, failing that one thing removes the reason to keep it.

**Data loss is the most permanent.** `NEG_DATALOSS` = 692 (2.67%, 1.99★). `14508743492` (#25596, 2026-09-04, gb, 1★) is the most forensic report in the corpus — an iCloud merge that migrated eleven list names and zero reminders, with nothing in Recently Deleted.

**The widget is a double-edged surface.** `NEG_WIDGET_BUG` = 684 (2.64%, 2.61★) — split between staleness and the interactive checkbox completing tasks by accident. `14444116484` (#25165, 2026-08-18, us, 1★) — "There needs to be an option to turn off the ability to check off reminders via the widget without opening the app. Reminders are constantly being checked off by accident". `14183465356` (#23500, 2026-06-14, jp, 4★) — "ロック画面に表示してると知らないうちに触れていて実行済みにされてしまう" *[with it on the lock screen I touch it without noticing and it gets marked done]*.

**Sharing is the least reliable feature relative to how much it is loved.** `PR_SHARED` = 617 (2.38%, 4.77★) against `NEG_SHARED_BUG` = 408 (1.57%, 2.25★) — a roughly 3:2 ratio, far worse than any other capability. `14461523864` (#25268, 2026-08-23, se, 1★) — "I update grocery list, wife sees old version hours later. Creates irritation and lost time."

## 3.6 Free, built-in, and what that buys

Covered as a competitive fact in §0.1 and as money in Part 5. The finding worth isolating here: **`PR_BUILTIN` (555, 2.14%, 4.51★) has a *lower* mean than `PR_FREE` (271, 1.04%, 4.79★)**. Being free is unambiguously good; being built-in comes with an expectation attached — several `PR_BUILTIN` reviews are of the form "it's Apple, it should be better". `10403491769` (#3027, 2023-09-24, us, 4★) titles itself "The definition of 'passable'".

**Grocery is the killer app inside the killer app — in some markets only.** `PR_GROCERY` = 1,371 (5.28%) globally, but 8.25% in the US, 8.49% in Australia, 12.79% in Austria — and **0.16% in China, 0.00% in Taiwan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Vietnam and the UAE** (§6.5). The automatic categorisation is what people name, and it is also what breaks (§3.7).

## 3.7 Friction, and the AI that made it worse

`NEG_CONFUSING` = 1,102 (4.25%, 3.02★) and `NEG_TOOMANYTAPS` = 481 (1.85%, 2.92★). The recurring specifics are date/time entry (`NEG_DATEPICKER` = 207), reordering (`NEG_SORT` = 390) and search (`NEG_SEARCH` = 261).

**Search is a trust failure, not a convenience failure.** `14435543371` (#25098, 2026-08-16, us, 3★) — "List items will often stop showing up in searches until you to mark them complete then incomplete again". `14270320039` (#24066, 2026-07-06, gb, 2★) — "don't rely on it because the search doesn't work to find items… it constantly shows 0 items when I know there are lots". The most precise is `14464030991` (#25283, 2026-08-23, us, 3★) — "All searches return 0 found items unless the item was recently edited or had a recent due date."

**Apple Intelligence grocery categorisation is the only feature in this corpus that is net-negative.** `NEG_GROCERY` = 270 (1.04%, 2.56★) + `NEG_APPLEINT` = 132 (0.51%, 2.67★) against `PR_APPLEINT` = 93 (0.36%, 4.88★). It also **rises over time**: `NEG_GROCERY` runs 0.76% (2026Q1) → 1.77% (2026Q2) → 1.89% (2026Q3) and `NEG_APPLEINT` 0.31% → 0.68% → 1.40%.

`14382720714` (#24751, 2026-08-03, gb, 4★) — "I typed 'eggs' into my 'Baking' section and it suggested moving 'eggs' to Baking! I did, and it made a new Baking section." `14282741871` (#24140, 2026-07-09, us, 2★) — "creating a 'Condiments & Sauces' section and automatically moving 'pull-up bar' to there is less than helpful. **At least provide a setting where we can turn off your idiotic AI features.**" `14193806237` (#23573, 2026-06-17, de, 1★) — "sortiert Batterien als Lebensmittel" *[sorts batteries as groceries]*. `14470208689` (#25322, 2026-08-25, de, 2★) — "Intelligente Sortierung der Listen funktioniert nur auf Englisch" *[smart list sorting only works in English]*.

**The transferable rule: automatic organisation that cannot be turned off converts a loved feature into a one-star review.**

## 3.8 Requests, ranked

`U_REQ_ANY` = 5,343 (20.59%, 3.70★). The top requests by count:

| Request | n | % | Mean | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `REQ_CALENDAR` — show/edit alongside calendar | 953 | 3.67% | 3.98★ | **shipped** — collapses to 0.85% by 2026Q3 (§7.3) |
| `REQ_ALARM` — alarm-strength alerts | 668 | 2.57% | 3.50★ | **shipped** — flips to praise from 2025Q4 (§0.4) |
| `REQ_CUSTOM` — colours, themes, fonts, icons | 640 | 2.47% | 3.41★ | open |
| `REQ_FLEXFREQ` — richer repeat rules | 364 | 1.40% | 3.44★ | **open — the #1 habit blocker** |
| `REQ_NOTIF_CTRL` — control over when/how it nags | 331 | 1.28% | 3.54★ | open |
| `REQ_INTEGRATION` — Mail, Messages, third-party, AI | 293 | 1.13% | 3.65★ | open |
| `REQ_WIDGET` — more/better widgets | 274 | 1.06% | 3.73★ | partly shipped |
| `REQ_UNDO` — undo an accidental completion/delete | 212 | 0.82% | 2.95★ | open |
| `REQ_ATTACH` — files, PDFs, richer text | 196 | 0.76% | 3.69★ | open |
| `REQ_SNOOZE` — custom snooze intervals | 196 | 0.76% | 3.42★ | **regressed** (§7.4) |
| `REQ_PROGRESS` — see progress/history | 180 | 0.69% | 4.03★ | open |
| `REQ_SUBTASK` — deeper nesting | 173 | 0.67% | 3.79★ | partly shipped |
| `REQ_TAGS` — tags, incl. across shared lists | 163 | 0.63% | 3.76★ | partly shipped |
| `REQ_SEARCH` — search inside a list | 120 | 0.46% | 3.78★ | open |
| `REQ_REWARD` — a payoff on completion | 119 | 0.46% | 4.38★ | open |
| `REQ_HABITMODE` — an explicit habit mode | 109 | 0.42% | 4.05★ | open |

**`REQ_FLEXFREQ` is the request that most directly blocks habit use** and the one most often stated with a concrete rule the app cannot express: repeat *after completion* rather than on a fixed date; every 3 days; Monday and Friday only; N times then stop; every 84 hours. `14392999764` (#24824, 2026-08-06, us, 1★) lays out the oil-change case in full and names two competitors that do it — Palm To-Do and Microsoft Tasks. `14498556910` (#25514, 2026-09-01, us, 3★) — "I cannot create a reminder that repeats every 3.5 days or every 84 hours… which would help with managing meds, maintenance schedules".

## 3.9 Solicited reviews and what the prompt costs

`SOLICIT` = 142 (0.55%, **mean 2.30★**) — reviewers who say the in-app review prompt is why they are writing, and are angry about it. 83 of the 142 are one-star (58.5%, segment rate). `14358616211` (#24587, 2026-07-28, us, 1★) — "STOP interrupting work with forced reviews. Stop. You know how often I use this program. I keep coming back, which you also know." `14431412737` (#25066, 2026-08-15, us, 1★) — "I don't care about your metrics you bugged me at the wrong moment".

**This is a measurable, self-inflicted rating cost**: had those 142 reviews not been written, the corpus mean would rise from 3.9399★ to 3.9489★. Small — but it is 100% attributable to the prompt, and it is a caution for any product that solicits ratings in-flow.

## 3.10 Switching, both directions

`U_SWITCH_ANY` = 1,519 (5.85%, 3.64★).

| Direction | Code | n | % | Mean |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Came **to** Reminders from another app | `SW_FROM_3P` | 371 | 1.43% | 4.71★ |
| Came from paper / a physical planner | `SW_PAPER` | 315 | 1.21% | 4.53★ |
| Names a competitor (either direction) | `SW_NAMED` | 574 | 2.21% | 3.63★ |
| **Considering** leaving | `SW_CONSIDER` | 296 | 1.14% | 2.02★ |
| Has **left** or is leaving | `SW_TO_3P` | 144 | 0.55% | 2.19★ |
| Left specifically over habit/routine handling | `HAB_SWITCH_OUT` | 46 | 0.18% | 2.00★ |

**Inbound (371 + 315 = 686) outnumbers outbound (144 + 46 = 190) by roughly 3.6:1**, and inbound reviewers rate 4.71★ against outbound 2.19★. `SW_PAPER` is the quietly large one: paper, not another app, is what Reminders most often replaces. `14448405754` (#25195, 2026-08-19, fr, 5★) — "Indispensable pour les courses. Évite la liste papier qui reste à la maison" *[indispensable for shopping. Avoids the paper list that stays at home]*.

**Competitors named, mechanically (§9.F):** Google Tasks/Keep/Calendar 77, Todoist 59, Microsoft To Do 37, Notion 28, Things 26, TickTick 17, Structured 11, Any.do 4, **dedicated habit apps 3**.

## 3.11 Platform reach as a constraint

`NEG_PLATFORM` = 465 (1.79%, 2.78★) and `REQ_PLATFORM` = 66 (0.25%). The corpus contains repeated, specific loss of users to cross-platform needs: Windows, a web client, Android family members, work environments. `12128071433` (#14309, 2024-12-31, in, 1★) — "I had to move away from using reminders app because the web version won't even have a basic sort feature." `12143261633` (#14393, 2025-01-04, ee, 2★) — "over 2 months of usage synchronization got completely broken several times… we switched back to Microsoft To Do for shared shopping list."

**For a competitor this is the one structural weakness Apple will not fix: Reminders cannot follow a user onto a non-Apple device, and shared lists break at the family boundary when one member is on Android.**

# PART 4 — RATINGS ANALYSIS

## 4.1 The distribution

| Stars | n | % | Cumulative |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 5★ | 15,241 | 58.73% | 58.73% |
| 4★ | 3,079 | 11.86% | 70.59% |
| 3★ | 2,316 | 8.92% | 79.52% |
| 2★ | 1,460 | 5.63% | 85.15% |
| 1★ | 3,855 | 14.85% | 100.00% |

**Corpus mean 3.9399★ against a public mean of 4.8116★ across 2,848,718 ratings (§6.7).** The shape is the classic text-review J-curve: a large five-star mass and a one-star tail nearly three times the two-star band. The 1★ bar is the one that carries information, because writing 400 words to give one star requires a grievance.

## 4.2 Themes by star band

Share within each band (segment rates; a review can appear in several rows):

| Code | 1★ (n=3,855) | 2★ (1,460) | 3★ (2,316) | 4★ (3,079) | 5★ (15,241) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `NEG_UPDATE` | 22.75% | 18.84% | 11.83% | 4.94% | 1.14% |
| `NEG_BUG` | 19.27% | 16.16% | 9.76% | 5.29% | 0.92% |
| `NEG_NOTIF_FAIL` | 14.27% | 6.99% | 3.80% | 1.79% | 0.35% |
| `NEG_DATALOSS` | 10.22% | 5.68% | 4.15% | 2.08% | 0.36% |
| `NEG_CRASH` | 9.29% | 6.30% | 3.24% | 1.33% | 0.35% |
| `NEG_SYNC` | 7.83% | 7.67% | 4.84% | 1.98% | 0.47% |
| `NEG_CONFUSING` | 7.55% | 10.75% | 8.33% | 5.16% | 1.98% |
| `REQ_CALENDAR` | 1.22% | 3.90% | 6.69% | 9.74% | 2.59% |
| `REQ_ALARM` | 2.62% | 4.38% | 5.40% | 5.07% | 1.46% |
| `REQ_CUSTOM` | 2.88% | 3.63% | 5.44% | 5.36% | 1.21% |
| `HAB_DAILY` | 2.57% | 3.84% | 4.75% | 7.60% | 13.17% |
| `SEG_MEMORY` | 0.39% | 0.34% | 0.99% | 4.58% | 13.17% |
| `DEPEND` | 2.78% | 2.74% | 2.55% | 2.79% | 9.98% |
| `PR_ORGANISE` | 0.23% | 0.55% | 1.55% | 5.98% | 16.00% |
| `PR_GENERIC` | 0.47% | 1.64% | 4.40% | 12.63% | 29.60% |

**Three patterns worth naming.**

1. **`NEG_UPDATE` is monotone and steep** — 22.75% → 1.14%. Regression is the single best predictor of a low star rating in this corpus, ahead of any missing feature.
2. **`REQ_CALENDAR`, `REQ_ALARM` and `REQ_CUSTOM` peak in the 3★ and 4★ bands, not the 1★ band.** Feature requests come from *satisfied* users. The people who want more are not the people who are leaving (§0.7).
3. **`DEPEND` at 2.78% of 1★ reviews** is the most uncomfortable number here: people who say they cannot live without the app *and* give it one star. That is the signature of dependency plus betrayal, and it is why §0.2 treats reliability as existential rather than cosmetic.

## 4.3 Five-star reviews — 15,241 (58.73%)

81.41% of five-star reviews carry at least one praise code (12,408 of 15,241, segment rate); 29.60% carry only `PR_GENERIC`. The named reasons, in order, are organisation (16.00%), memory relief (13.17%), daily-habit use (13.17%), dependency (9.98%), ease (9.26%), notifications that work (6.84%) and groceries (6.77%).

**9.81% of five-star reviews (1,495) also carry a negative code.** These are "love it, but" reviews and they are the richest source of roadmap signal in the corpus, because the complaint is uncontaminated by anger.

## 4.4 Four-star reviews — 3,079 (11.86%)

**52.84% of four-star reviews carry a feature request** (1,627 of 3,079, segment rate) against 11.74% of five-star and 14.01% of one-star reviews. **Four stars in this corpus means "one thing away".** The most common single missing thing was calendar integration (9.74% of the band) — which shipped, and which is why this band's composition changed in 2025 (§7.3).

## 4.5 Three-star reviews — 2,316 (8.92%)

The genuinely mixed band, and the most diagnostically useful. Over-represented against global rates: `NEG_UI` (4.36% vs 1.41% global, **3.1×**), `NEG_TOOMANYTAPS` (5.44% vs 1.85%, 2.9×), `NEG_SORT` (4.58% vs 1.50%, 3.1×), `NEG_FEATURELESS` (5.14% vs 1.63%, 3.2×), `NEG_WIDGET_BUG` (6.48% vs 2.64%, 2.5×).

**Three stars is where friction lives.** Not broken, not missing — awkward. `14464030991` (#25283, 2026-08-23, us, 3★) and `14435543371` (#25098, 2026-08-16, us, 3★) are typical: long-term users, still using it, documenting a specific degradation.

## 4.6 One- and two-star reviews — 5,315 (20.48%)

**69.48% are reliability reports** (3,693, segment rate) and 21.67% say something broke in an update (1,152). The remaining fifth splits between confusion (7.55% of 1★), the permission nag of §0.5, and content the taxonomy classes as `NOISE` (4.18% of 1★ — joke reviews, test posts, off-topic).

The most important asymmetry: **`NEG_NOTIF_FAIL` is 14.27% of one-star reviews and 0.35% of five-star reviews, a 41× ratio.** No other code separates the bands so sharply.

## 4.7 Rating-versus-text contradictions

`CONTRA_RATING` = 496 (1.91%) marks reviews whose stars and text disagree. The split is lopsided: **348 are five-star reviews whose text is negative or neutral**, 88 are one-star reviews whose text is positive.

Both directions are real and both are disclosed rather than silently dropped:
- `14375570423` (#24703, 2026-08-01, ca, 5★) — "Just doesn't get things done for me :(" — five stars, stated failure.
- `12605386823` (#16584, 2025-05-01, jp, 1★) — "なんかスマホ持ってても気が付かない" *[somehow I don't notice even with the phone on me]* — one star for a notification being missable, from someone describing ADHD.

**Effect on the numbers.** 348 five-star reviews with negative text means the corpus mean slightly *overstates* satisfaction, in the same direction as — and much smaller than — the non-response bias of §6.7. Theme counts are unaffected, because codes are assigned from text, never from stars. **No finding in this report is derived from star rating alone.**

# PART 5 — MONEY: WHO PAYS, FOR WHAT, AND WHY NOT HERE

> Reminders is free, pre-installed, has no in-app purchase, no trial, no paywall and no ads (§2.3). This part therefore does **not** analyse conversion. It analyses the two money flows this corpus *can* evidence: money that leaves to third-party apps, and money that stops leaving.

## 5.1 The monetisation model

There isn't one. The only monetary dependency anywhere in the corpus is iCloud storage, named by 9 reviewers (`MON_PAID_ICLOUD` = 0.03%, ignore-by-default). One of those nine, `14193949220` (#23575, 2026-06-17, us, 1★), mistakenly believes list sharing is paywalled. It is not, and no other review makes the claim.

## 5.2 The six money codes

| Code | n | % of 25,951 | Mean | Band |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `MON_FREE_VALUE` — free/built-in is why they use it | 387 | 1.49% | 4.80★ | Meaningful |
| `MON_REFUSE_PAY` — says don't pay for this category | 97 | 0.37% | 4.56★ | Weak |
| `MON_PAID_3P` — pays or paid a third party | 68 | 0.26% | 4.18★ | Weak |
| `MON_CANCEL_3P` — cancelled a paid app for this one | 37 | 0.14% | 4.84★ | Weak |
| `MON_WOULD_PAY` — would pay for something | 11 | 0.04% | 2.91★ | Ignore by default |
| `MON_PAID_ICLOUD` — mentions paying for iCloud | 9 | 0.03% | 3.22★ | Ignore by default |
| **`U_MONEY_ANY`** | **488** | **1.88%** | **4.62★** | **Meaningful** |

**Only 1.88% of reviewers mention money at all**, and when they do it is overwhelmingly to say they are not spending any.

## 5.3 What paid third-party users say, and what brought them back

`MON_PAID_3P` = 68 is the only direct purchase evidence in the corpus, and it is purchase evidence for **competitors**. These reviewers had a paid habit — OmniFocus, Things, Todoist, AnyList, TickTick, Notion — and are describing either why they still pay or why they stopped.

**Why they stopped paying** (`MON_CANCEL_3P` = 37, mean 4.84★ — the highest mean of any money code): capability caught up, and free won. `10514522309` (#4039, 2023-10-25, us, 5★) — "I've been an omnifocus user for years and happily paid the subscription fee, but lately… the new version is VERY capable and does everything i need. And it's free". `12450118186` (#15881, 2025-03-22, de, 4★) — "Ich habe jahrelang Things genutzt, bin aber nun endgültig umgestiegen… So reicht dann diese App absolut und kostet nichts" *[I used Things for years but have now switched for good… this app is completely enough and costs nothing]*.

**Why some still pay** — the reason is always a single specific capability, never overall quality. `12046765952` (#13933, 2024-12-10, br, 3★) — "The widget doesn't show the date of the task/reminder. **I pay Todoist to have that.**" `13241933504` (#19159, 2025-10-09, us, 4★) — "it does not have the same customizability as an app like Todoist… Apple Reminders is limited in how you filter your to do".

**This is the clearest commercial signal in the whole corpus: people pay for one missing capability, not for a better app.**

## 5.4 Willingness to pay, examined directly

`MON_WOULD_PAY` = 11 (0.04%) is below threshold and is reported qualitatively. Its **mean rating is 2.91★** — the only money code below the corpus mean — because nine of the eleven are frustrated users threatening to spend money elsewhere, not offers to spend money here.

The single most useful sentence about pricing in 25,951 reviews is `14522067015` (#25682, 2026-09-07, us, 5★):

> "Reminders has gotten so good I can't fathom my anyone would pay $100 a year to use another app. If there was another high-quality Reminders app that I could just pay for once, I would consider it. Every single app as a huge subscription prize which makes zero sense for the level of this is."

Three things follow, and all three should be treated as hypotheses to test rather than conclusions:
1. **An annual subscription at ~$100 is explicitly rejected** by a user who is otherwise enthusiastic about the category.
2. **A one-time purchase is explicitly entertained** by the same user.
3. **The bar is set by a free incumbent that is improving.** `PR_IMPROVED` = 984 (3.79%, 4.70★) — reviewers notice and say so.

**What this corpus cannot tell you:** any price point, any conversion rate, any elasticity. 87 reviews (0.34%) name a price at all, and nearly all of those are naming a competitor's price as a reason to avoid it.

## 5.5 Upgrade barriers, reframed as adoption barriers

For a paid entrant, the barriers evidenced here are:

| Barrier | Evidence | n | % |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| "It's already on my phone and free" | `U_FREE_VALUE` | 902 | 3.48% |
| "It does enough" | `PR_ENOUGH` | 645 | 2.49% |
| "Simplicity is the feature; more would be worse" | `PR_SIMPLE` | 1,049 | 4.04% |
| "It's better than the paid ones I tried" | `PR_BETTER_THAN` | 722 | 2.78% |
| Explicit anti-subscription stance | `MON_REFUSE_PAY` | 97 | 0.37% |
| Ecosystem lock-in (Siri, Calendar, Watch, CarPlay) | `PR_ECOSYSTEM` + `PR_INTEGRATION` | 934 | 3.60% |

`11579759798` (#11473, 2024-08-06, us, 5★) states the whole barrier in two sentences — "I've gone through many to do/task apps and I always felt that things became over complicated and plus I was paying for the subscriptions. This app is free and very simple."

## 5.6 What cannot be claimed here

- No conversion rate, ARPU, LTV or retention figure. The data does not contain purchase state.
- No claim that `MON_WOULD_PAY` = 11 represents 0.04% willingness-to-pay in the population. It represents 0.04% *of people who wrote a review*, which is 0.911% of people who rated, which is an unknown fraction of people who use the app.
- No claim about what Apple earns. Reminders exists to sell hardware and iCloud; that is a strategic inference, not a review finding, and it is stated here only to mark that it was *not* derived from the corpus.

## 6.3 United States — 9,197 reviews (35.44%), mean 4.01★ — eligible

Over a third of the corpus. Above corpus average on almost every praise code and **below** it on reliability (21.59% vs 24.12%).

| Theme | US | Global | Read |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `PR_GROCERY` | 8.25% | 5.28% | **1.6× the global rate** — the grocery list is a US-centric hit |
| `SEG_MEMORY` | 10.55% | 8.45% | memory framing is strongest here |
| `HAB_DAILY` | 11.99% | 9.66% | |
| `HAB_MED` | 2.51% | 1.44% | **1.7×** — medication is a US-heavy use |
| `PR_SIRI` | 3.21% | 2.16% | |
| `U_SWITCH_ANY` | 7.13% | 5.85% | most switching talk of any large market |
| `REQ_CALENDAR` | 2.56% | 3.67% | below global — US reviewers asked earlier and got it |
| `U_HABIT_TRACK_GAP` | 4.11% | 4.48% | slightly **below** global |

**The US is where the product works best and where the habit gap is felt least.** That is a caution for a habit product built on US-only research: the strongest demand signal is elsewhere (§6.5).

## 6.4 China mainland — 1,288 reviews (4.96%), mean 3.59★ — eligible

The most important storefront in this report for the decision at hand, and the one with the widest gap to its public rating (**+1.30★**; public 4.892★ over 151,134 ratings).

| Theme | CN | Global | Read |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `U_RELIABILITY` | 36.41% | 24.12% | **1.5×** — reliability dominates Chinese reviews |
| `U_HABIT_TRACK_GAP` | **9.01%** | 4.48% | **2.0× — the highest of any large storefront** |
| `PR_GROCERY` | **0.16%** | 5.28% | the grocery feature is effectively absent here |
| `PR_SHARED` | 0.23% | 2.38% | |
| `HAB_MED` | 0.00% | 1.44% | zero medication reviews |
| `NEG_UPDATE` | 8.70% | 6.75% | |

**Chinese reviewers use Reminders as a 打卡 (check-in / streak) tool and say so explicitly.** `13672266551` (#20688, 2026-01-25, cn, 5★) — "试了各种打卡软件 发现还是自带的最好哈哈… 反正我把提醒事项当打卡记录软件好久了" *[I tried all kinds of check-in apps and found the built-in one is still the best… anyway I've used Reminders as a check-in record app for ages]*. `13400477405` (#19936, 2025-11-15, cn, 5★) — "每天打卡…不仅是提醒事项，也是每天向着标杆直跑的指示牌" *[daily check-in… not just reminders, but a signpost for running toward the goal each day]*. `13962894485` (#22046, 2026-04-16, cn, 4★) supplies the exact failure — a check-in that does not show as complete causes duplicate check-ins.

**This is the sharpest product finding in Part 6: the market with the least interest in Reminders' flagship feature (groceries) has the most interest in the feature it does not have (streak tracking).**

## 6.5 Where the habit-tracking gap is loudest

Eligible storefronts by `U_HABIT_TRACK_GAP` share (global 4.48%):

| Storefront | n | Gap share | vs global |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Singapore | 87 | 10.34% | 2.3× |
| **China mainland** | **1,288** | **9.01%** | **2.0×** |
| Philippines | 119 | 7.56% | 1.7× |
| Norway | 105 | 6.67% | 1.5× |
| **India** | **527** | **6.64%** | **1.5×** |
| New Zealand | 76 | 6.58% | 1.5× |

Only China, India, Korea and Japan among these carry enough reviews to be more than suggestive; Singapore, the Philippines, Norway, New Zealand and Ukraine are eligible but small, and their rates should be treated as directional.

Japan supplies the most articulate statement of the use case in the corpus — `13970379637` (#22100, 2026-04-18, jp, 5★): "習慣化って最低でも3ヶ月以上かかります。その良い習慣を身につけるためにリマインダーはとても役に立ちます" *[habit formation takes at least three months. Reminders is very useful for acquiring that good habit]*. Korea supplies the free-versus-paid verdict — `11187136900` (#9119, 2024-04-22, kr, 5★): "돈 아끼고자 기본 내장으로 되어있길래 써보는데, 유로 어플보다 훨씬 나은 것 같아요" *[I tried the built-in one to save money, and it seems much better than the paid apps]*.

## 6.6 Grocery is a Western-market feature

`PR_GROCERY` global 5.28%, but the spread across eligible storefronts is extreme:

| High | | Low | |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| Austria | 12.79% | Turkey | 0.00% |
| Finland | 10.34% | Singapore | 0.00% |
| New Zealand | 9.21% | Saudi Arabia | 0.00% |
| Australia | 8.49% | Peru | 0.00% |
| United States | 8.25% | Greece | 0.00% |
| Ireland | 8.06% | Egypt | 0.00% |
| Germany | 5.60% | UAE | 0.00% |
| | | Taiwan | 0.00% |
| | | China mainland | 0.16% |

Two mechanisms are visible in the text and should not be conflated. **First, the automatic categoriser is English-first** — `14470208689` (#25322, 2026-08-25, de, 2★) — "Intelligente Sortierung der Listen funktioniert nur auf Englisch" *[smart list sorting only works in English]*. **Second, shopping-list-on-phone may simply be a different behaviour in these markets**; the corpus cannot distinguish the two, and no causal claim is made.

## 6.7 High-volume markets, and the corpus-versus-public gap

**Definition, disclosed:** no spend data was available, so the high-volume group is defined by **public rating count** from `Tools/native_ratings.json` — a volume proxy, explicitly **not** downloads and **not** revenue.

The ten highest-volume storefronts (US, DE, CN, JP, CA, BR, GB, MX, FR, IT) hold **17,548 corpus reviews (67.62%)**.

**The gap is the headline of this section.** Across the 144 storefronts in the corpus:

| | Value |
|---|---|
| Public ratings | **2,848,718** |
| Public weighted mean | **4.8116★** |
| Corpus text reviews | 25,951 |
| Corpus mean | **3.9399★** |
| **Gap** | **+0.8717★** |
| Text reviews as share of ratings | **0.911%** |

Every storefront shows a positive gap. The widest are **Russia (+1.79★)** and **China (+1.30★)**; the narrowest are **Mexico (+0.49★)** and **France (+0.61★)**. Russia's gap is the largest because its corpus reviews are dominated by the §0.5 permission-banner wave (`NEG_UPDATE` = 27.73% of Russian reviews against 6.75% globally, and `U_RELIABILITY` = 50.67%).

**Read every negative rate in this report as an upper bound.** A reader who takes `U_RELIABILITY` = 24.12% as "a quarter of Reminders users have a broken app" will be badly wrong; the correct reading is "a quarter of the 0.911% of raters who wrote text reported something broken."

## 6.8 Storefront is not language

Script family, derived mechanically from title+body (§9.F), not from storefront:

| Script | n | % |
|---|---:|---:|
| Latin | 21,586 | 83.18% |
| Chinese (Han, no kana) | 1,705 | 6.57% |
| Cyrillic | 900 | 3.47% |
| Japanese (kana present) | 898 | 3.46% |
| Korean (Hangul) | 482 | 1.86% |
| Thai | 124 | 0.48% |
| Arabic | 123 | 0.47% |
| Hebrew | 67 | 0.26% |
| Greek | 23 | 0.09% |
| Tamil | 1 | 0.00% |
| No letters (emoji/punctuation only) | 42 | 0.16% |

**16.66% of the corpus is non-Latin script.** Latin script spans English, Spanish, German, French, Portuguese, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Swedish, Turkish, Vietnamese, Czech, Danish, Norwegian, Indonesian, Romanian, Slovak, Lithuanian, Catalan and more, so "Latin" is not "English".

A per-review hand language tag was recorded while reading, but in early batches it sometimes captured the storefront rather than the language. **That field is therefore treated as a reading aid only and is used for no quantified claim in this report.** The mechanical script table above is what every language statement rests on. (This is disclosed rather than silently corrected; the tag is still shown in Part 10 marked as unverified.)

## 6.9 Storefronts below 50 reviews — limited evidence

94 storefronts, 893 reviews (3.44%), pooled mean **4.21★** — higher than the corpus mean, consistent with smaller markets producing fewer grievance-driven reviews. Largest are Nigeria (49), Kazakhstan (45), Guatemala (43), Hungary (42), Costa Rica (35), Slovakia (34), Pakistan (33), Bulgaria (32).

**No standalone claim is made about any of them.** Their reviews are included in every global figure. Where one contains a notable individual observation it is cited as an individual review, never as a country pattern — for example `12648138253` (#16752, 2025-05-12, lt, 5★) from Lithuania (28 reviews, below threshold) on progress tracking, quoted in §0.3 as one person's statement and not as evidence about Lithuania.

# PART 7 — TIME-TREND ANALYSIS

## 7.1 Method, and the one era that cannot be trusted

Eras are cut at the mid-September release boundary, which is when Apple ships major iOS versions. **There is no version field**, so these are calendar windows, not release cohorts.

| Era | Window | n | % | Mean | Votes/review | Median body |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **E1** pre-iOS 17 | 2021-09-21 → 2023-09-17 | 2,815 | 10.85% | **2.419★** | **0.891** | **115** |
| **E2** iOS 17 | 2023-09-18 → 2024-09-15 | 9,431 | 36.34% | 4.113★ | 0.067 | 87 |
| **E3** iOS 18 | 2024-09-16 → 2025-09-14 | 6,357 | 24.50% | 4.154★ | 0.066 | 78 |
| **E4** iOS 26 | 2025-09-15 → 2026-09-18 | 7,348 | 28.31% | 4.115★ | 0.061 | 76 |

**E1 is not comparable to E2–E4 and must not be read as a trend.** Three independent signatures say so:
1. **Volume.** ~100 reviews/month through August 2023, then 515 in September 2023 and 900+/month after. The product did not become 9× more discussed in one month.
2. **Helpful votes.** E1 carries **13× the votes per review** of every later era (0.891 vs 0.061–0.067). Listings that retain old reviews retain the *most-voted* ones.
3. **Length.** E1's median body is 115 characters against 76–87 later — long, argued reviews survive; "great app" does not.

Together these are the signature of a feed that preserved a helpful-vote-ranked subset of pre-September-2023 reviews and dropped the rest. Helpful votes skew negative, which fully explains E1's 2.419★. **Every era comparison below is stated on E2→E4, and §9.D re-runs the headlines with E1 excluded entirely.**

## 7.2 Theme movement across E2 → E4 (share within era)

| Code | E2 | E3 | E4 | Movement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `PR_INTEGRATION` | 1.02% | 2.08% | 2.76% | **rising, 2.7×** |
| `PR_PROGRESS` | 2.59% | 3.40% | 4.59% | **rising, 1.8×** |
| `REQ_ALARM` | 1.97% | 2.52% | 3.46% | **rising, 1.8×** |
| `NEG_TOOMANYTAPS` | 1.13% | 2.27% | 2.75% | **rising, 2.4×** |
| `PR_RELIABLE` | 1.74% | 2.03% | 2.95% | rising |
| `SEG_MEMORY` | 8.57% | 9.45% | 10.33% | rising |
| `NEG_SORT` | 0.86% | 1.90% | 2.15% | rising, 2.5× |
| `NEG_GROCERY` | 0.89% | 1.13% | 1.55% | rising |
| `REQ_CALENDAR` | 4.99% | 4.51% | **1.14%** | **falling, 4.4×** |
| `NEG_WIDGET_BUG` | 5.31% | 1.04% | 0.98% | **falling, 5.4×** |
| `HAB_NOHIST` | 1.40% | 0.93% | 0.38% | falling |
| `NEG_SUBTASK` | 0.94% | 1.13% | 0.53% | falling |
| `PR_ENOUGH` | 3.97% | 1.92% | 1.48% | **falling, 2.7×** |
| `U_HABIT_TRACK_GAP` | 4.39% | 4.55% | 4.02% | **flat** |
| `U_FREE_VALUE` | 3.60% | 3.42% | 3.22% | flat |

## 7.3 Two requests that were shipped, and what that looks like in the data

**Calendar integration.** `REQ_CALENDAR` was the single most-requested feature in the corpus (953, 3.67%). Quarterly it runs 5.19% (2025Q1) → 3.69% (Q2) → **1.19% (Q3)** → 1.35% → 1.91% → 0.86% → **0.85% (2026Q3)**. `PR_INTEGRATION` moves the opposite way over the same quarters: 1.25% → 2.39% → **4.56%** → 2.98% → 2.75% → 2.59% → 2.44%. Monthly, the crossover is **June 2025**: `REQ_CALENDAR` 4.12% → 2.13%, `PR_INTEGRATION` 2.06% → 4.26%.

**This is what a shipped request looks like: the ask collapses, the praise rises, and neither returns to baseline.** `13287024296` (#19392, 2025-10-19, dk, 5★) — "The integration of Reminders into Calendar was the feature tipping point for me… has me using Reminders, now, on a daily basis." `13909164704` (#21749, 2026-04-01, us, 5★) — "Each task with a due date assigned automatically shows up in the Calendar App. The integration saves a lot of time."

**Urgent alarms.** Covered in §0.4. `REQ_ALARM` rises 1.97% → 2.52% → 3.46% across E2→E4 while flipping from request to praise — the rarer pattern where shipping a feature *increases* mentions because people now talk about using it.

**Caution on both.** No version field exists. The June 2025 crossover precedes the September 2025 iOS release by three months, so it may reflect a point release, a beta cohort, or WWDC-driven awareness. **The correlation is stated; the cause is not.**

## 7.4 What got worse

**Interactive widgets were an E2 crisis that was fixed.** `NEG_WIDGET_BUG` spikes to **5.31% in E2** — a period when tapping a widget checkbox completed the wrong task or the widget showed stale data — then falls to 1.04% and 0.98%. It is the clearest resolved regression in the corpus. A residue remains as a *design* complaint rather than a bug: `14444116484` (#25165, 2026-08-18, us, 1★) still wants the checkbox disabled.

**Friction is rising while reliability improves.** `NEG_TOOMANYTAPS` 1.13% → 2.27% → 2.75% and `NEG_SORT` 0.86% → 1.90% → 2.15%, against falling crash and sync rates. As the app gained sections, columns, tags, smart lists and templates, the cost of a simple edit went up. `PR_ENOUGH` falling 2.7× (3.97% → 1.48%) is the same story from the other side: fewer people now say it does exactly enough.

**Snooze regressed.** `REQ_SNOOZE` = 196 (0.76%) and `NEG_NOSNOOZE` = 26 (0.10%) include multiple reviewers saying a shorter snooze interval was **removed**. `14448920757` (#25202, 2026-08-20, us, 1★) — "getting rid of being able to snooze a reminder for 15 mins (as you could a few years ago) was diabolical."

**Apple Intelligence grocery sorting is deteriorating in reception** — `NEG_GROCERY` 0.76% (2026Q1) → 1.77% (Q2) → 1.89% (Q3); `NEG_APPLEINT` 0.31% → 0.68% → 1.40% (§3.7).

## 7.5 The three-month regression of 2026

Covered in §0.5. Quantified here for the record:

| Month | n | Mean | `NEG_UPDATE` | `NEG_BUG` | `NEG_NOTIF_NAG` |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2025-11 | 442 | 4.09★ | 5.20% | 2.26% | 0.45% |
| **2025-12** | 330 | **3.64★** | **22.73%** | **18.48%** | 2.73% |
| **2026-01** | 339 | **3.19★** | **38.94%** | **35.10%** | **6.78%** |
| **2026-02** | 305 | **3.41★** | **29.84%** | **26.56%** | 4.59% |
| 2026-03 | 665 | 4.17★ | 4.81% | 4.66% | 0.45% |

Three months, 974 reviews, mean 3.41★, 331 one- and two-star. **It recovered completely and quickly** — March 2026 returns to 4.17★ and the corpus ends at **4.34★ in September 2026**, its highest monthly mean on record.

## 7.6 What has not changed in five years

- **`U_HABIT_TRACK_GAP` is flat at 4.02–4.55% across E2, E3 and E4**, and 3.45–6.16% in every quarter since 2023Q4. Five years of the same requests: repeat-after-completion, skip, reset, history, progress.
- **`U_FREE_VALUE` is flat at 3.22–3.60%.** The free/built-in advantage is neither growing nor eroding.
- **`SEG_MEMORY` rises gently** (8.57% → 10.33%), consistent with an ageing, broadening user base rather than any product change.
- **`MON_WOULD_PAY` never exceeds 11 reviews in any cut of the data.**
